title: Freight Inspection Checklist Form
subtitle: Set the freight inspection scope, test readiness and requirement-level evidence, contain deficiencies, authorize status, and preserve qualified closeout.
description: An original, fillable freight inspection checklist form for controlling palletized, crated, or unitized freight shipment through inspection checklist identity, observations, evidence, decision, exceptions, escalation, completion, handoff, and final verification without replacing applicable requirements or professional review.
use_case: Use when a freight operations coordinator or qualified inspector must evaluate palletized, crated, or unitized freight shipment against the shipment record, carrier document, purchase order, and packing list and provide a traceable basis for release, restriction, hold, correction, or rejection.

sections.title: Freight inspection checklist identity and routing
sections.guidance: Anchor the record to the exact work, parties, locations, and source references.

fields.label: Pallet, crate, handling-unit, or seal ID

blocks.label: Responsible parties and route points
blocks.guidance: Preserve linkage to the shipment record, carrier document, purchase order, and packing list.

sections.title: Freight inspection scope, criteria, and readiness
sections.guidance: Define the exact population and review basis so inspection conclusions remain bounded.

fields.label: Palletized, Crated, Or Unitized Freight Shipment
Shipment Record, Carrier Document, Purchase Order, And Packing List

blocks.label: Freight readiness verification
items: Shipment, purchase order, and carrier references identify the same freight
Handling-unit count, piece count, weight, and dimensions are reconciled
Pallets, crates, wrap, bands, and labels support ordinary freight handling
Load distribution, blocking, bracing, and securement are assigned for review
Trailer number, seal number, carrier, driver, and appointment are recorded
Dock equipment and labor support the weight and handling configuration
Hazard, food, temperature, high-value, or special handling status is routed
Shortage, overage, damage, refused freight, and redelivery paths are defined
blocks.guidance: A failed readiness item must be resolved, excluded with rationale, or carried into the exception section.

sections.title: Freight requirement-level inspection results
sections.guidance: Record actual observations against explicit criteria and identify the evidence for each result.

blocks.label: Freight detailed inspection points
items: Shipment reference matches carrier document, purchase order, and packing list
Pallet, crate, and handling-unit count agrees with tendered quantity
Visible weight and dimension markings support the planned equipment
Pallet deck, crate panels, wrap, banding, and corner protection are intact
Labels remain readable and do not conflict across handling units
Seal number and trailer identity agree with dispatch records
Blocking, bracing, dunnage, and tiedowns appear suitable for the load configuration
No leakage, leaning, collapse, puncture, water exposure, or contamination is visible
Appointment, dock, liftgate, accessorial, and unloading needs are confirmed
A discrepancy is held for qualified review before tender, release, or disposition
blocks.guidance: Checkboxes indicate that the point was examined; the result table carries findings and evidence.

sections.title: Freight measurements and evidence package
sections.guidance: Preserve readings, instruments, identity, and evidence needed to reproduce the inspection decision.

blocks.label: Measurement, count, or verification log
blocks.guidance: Use the method applicable to Handling units, pieces, and verified weight and Pallet, crate, wrap, and seal condition.

blocks.label: Available inspection evidence
items: Carrier document and purchase-order reference
Origin pallet or crate condition photographs
Certified or operational weight record
Trailer and seal identity
Dock arrival, loading, departure, and delivery timestamps
Handling-unit scans at each transfer
Destination condition and shortage notation
Exception inspection and mitigation record

blocks.label: Inspection observations, sampling limitations, and evidence interpretation

fields.label: Inspection observations, sampling limitations, and evidence interpretation

sections.title: Freight exception, containment, and escalation
sections.guidance: Make the trigger, affected scope, immediate control, owner, deadline, and escalation reconstructable.

blocks.label: Freight exception indicators
items: Handling-unit or piece shortage, overage, or substitution
Visible crush, puncture, collapse, tilt, water, or contamination damage
Pallet, crate, wrap, banding, or securement is compromised
Trailer or seal identity differs from the shipment record
Weight, dimension, freight description, or equipment is inconsistent
Appointment is missed or consignee cannot unload
Freight is refused, partially accepted, or redirected
Temperature, food, hazardous, or special handling control is uncertain
Carrier document, purchase order, or packing list cannot be reconciled
Salvage, rework, return, or disposal instruction is unresolved
blocks.guidance: Select every observed condition; do not use a generic exception mark when the actual trigger is known.

sections.title: Freight inspection status and release decision
sections.guidance: Do not turn a checklist score into release when a critical exception or evidence gap remains.

sections.title: Freight inspection checklist closeout and accountable handoff
sections.guidance: Close only when outcome, remaining limitation, next action, evidence, and receiving ownership agree.

blocks.label: Final outcome, handoff, and record location
Record boundary and stop condition
blocks.guidance: Use this freight inspection checklist with the applicable customer commitment, carrier terms, site policy, and retention requirements. Do not infer acceptance or release from a signature alone; unresolved identity, count, condition, custody, or proof issues require an owner, escalation, and documented disposition.

blocks.label: Prepared, reviewed, and accepted

fields.label: Reviewed by shipping or receiving manager

blocks.guidance: A signature records accountability for the stated decision; it does not cure missing evidence or override a stop condition.
